_FLOW: THE WORK QUEUE — everything the archive has committed to and not yet done, sorted by the KIND OF LABOUR that resolves it. The taxonomy is the point: these three categories are not degrees of urgency, they are different work. Category 1 resolves by waiting and checking — the world does the labour and you observe the result. Category 2 resolves by sustained attention — a protocol exists and must be executed. Category 3 resolves by engineering — something must be built before the question can even be asked.

1.name: Registered predictions from applied theory
1.note: CHEAPEST AND MOST NEGLECTED. Four of the six resolve in September, three of those for under forty API calls, and two are fully automated by scripts already written. A prediction that goes unchecked is not a prediction; it is a note.

2.name: Experiments with registered hypotheses
2.note: Every one is pre-registered with declared failure conditions. Anyone can run any of them and the result is admissible on the same terms. One — depositing the CT-01 null — is low-cost and overdue: a conducted failure that exists only in outputs.

3.name: Unimplemented software builds
3.note: Two are blocking: the compression detector blocks the entire blog-recovery programme, and until it exists 'not previously deposited' is a claim this archive cannot make about its own work. One is pure yield with nothing blocking it: scoring the 356 seated captures on the five-stage PER chain.

the_ratio_restated: Nine designed studies against five conducted was the dashboard's figure. This queue shows the same imbalance from the other side: twenty-one open commitments, of which six cost almost nothing and are simply unchecked.
if_only_one_thing: Category 1. Four predictions resolve in September, two of them by running a script that already exists. The archive's credibility rests on resolved predictions — including the six that resolved WRONG — and six more are sitting one API call away.
invitation: Every item carries its blocker, its next action and its cost. Nothing here requires permission.

items.title: Zenodo's deletion export resumes after the cron fix
items.theory: A stoppage with an identified mechanism should end when the mechanism is repaired.
items.how: GET zenodo.org/api/exporter — a records-deleted.csv.gz version created after 2026-08-20 confirms; nothing by 2026-09-10 disconfirms and the explanation is incomplete.
items.stake: Confirms the mundane explanation BY PREDICTION rather than inference, which is a stronger position than the one argued from all evening.
items.requires: nothing — one unauthenticated GET

items.title: The crimson-hexagonal address stops naming Zenodo as host
items.theory: A composition layer reporting a stale state should update once the source surfaces propagate.
items.how: Re-run the address on Bing Copilot. If it still returns Zenodo as host a month after the archive's surfaces were updated, the local explanation fails and the ghost-host reading becomes live again.
items.stake: The withdrawn finding's only route back.
items.requires: nothing — one browser query, signed out

items.title: SPXI treatment raises archive source share on the UNPREFIXED address
items.theory: Inscribing the discriminating coordinates should alter composition-layer behaviour.
items.how: Re-run the prefix battery, signed out, same surfaces. Success: share above zero on the bare address and no merge parenthetical. Failure at 180 days is recorded as failure.
items.stake: #1535 declared itself an intervention. This is whether it executed.
items.requires: nothing — four browser queries, signed out, seated as captures

items.title: Second global cohort epoch
items.theory: A publication-year cohort should be monotonically non-decreasing; any decrease is erasure.
items.stake: The baseline's entire value is that a second epoch can exist.
items.requires: nothing — 37 unauthenticated API calls; scripts/peo_cohort_epoch.py already written

items.title: Second fixed-panel epoch
items.theory: Re-querying a frozen DOI set measures erasure directly; minting cannot mask it.
items.how: scripts/peo_panel_epoch.py — 404 rate is the erasure rate.
items.stake: First direct measurement of global erasure the archive has ever taken.
items.requires: nothing — 720 unauthenticated API calls; scripts/peo_panel_epoch.py already written
